nc4757ca893a.s: Since 2019, housing finance companies in India have been regulated by:
nc4757ca893a.x: Regulation of housing finance companies shifted to the RBI in 2019; the NHB remains the apex housing refinancer.

n5e2d3ca6546.s: The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC), set up in 1978, is a wholly-owned subsidiary of:
n5e2d3ca6546.x: DICGC is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the RBI, not the Finance Ministry; it insures bank deposits but not NBFC deposits.

nc5530db2655.s: The RBI's Banking Ombudsman Scheme, started on 14 June 1995, was framed under:
nc5530db2655.x: The quasi-judicial Banking Ombudsman scheme began on 14 June 1995 under Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act.

nc741ecf8ed4.s: The Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC), set up in 2010, is a:
o: Statutory body under the RBI Act
Statutory body under the SEBI Act
nc741ecf8ed4.x: FSDC is a non-statutory apex body set up in 2010 and chaired by the Union Finance Minister.

n345597a6caf.s: The FSLRC proposed a Unified Financial Agency merging SEBI, FMC, IRDA and:
n345597a6caf.x: The Unified Financial Agency was to merge SEBI, FMC, IRDA and PFRDA; the RBI was to keep banking and payments.

na598cb4b317.s: Mutual funds in India are regulated by:
na598cb4b317.x: SEBI regulates listed companies, intermediaries and mutual funds.

n1d6a3a473a5.s: On the dissolution of BIFR on 1 December 2016, its cases were transferred to:
n1d6a3a473a5.x: BIFR, constituted under SICA 1985, was dissolved on 1 December 2016 and its cases moved to NCLT/NCLAT under the IBC.

neea7d5a5d2b.s: Under the DPDP Rules, 2025, the Data Protection Board of India has how many members?
neea7d5a5d2b.x: The DPDP Rules, 2025 provide for a four-member Data Protection Board under the DPDP Act, 2023.

n62d3765514d.s: The chairperson of a sectoral regulator is removed, on grounds listed in the parent Act and after a hearing, by the:
o: President on a Supreme Court reference
n62d3765514d.x: Removal is by the Central Government only on grounds specified in the parent Act and after the person has been heard.

n14e3f437a66.s: Which body hears telecom disputes and appeals, separate from TRAI's regulatory role?
n14e3f437a66.x: TRAI regulates tariffs, interconnection and quality of service, while TDSAT handles telecom disputes and appeals.

naff4ec72f54.s: Which of the following pairs (regulator – function) is correctly matched?
o: AERA – Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
naff4ec72f54.x: PNGRB works under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas and regulates City Gas Distribution networks; it does not regulate electricity transmission.

nb44ecefe92a.s: After its introduction in the Lok Sabha in December 2025, the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill was:
o: Referred to a Joint Committee of Parliament
nb44ecefe92a.x: The VBSA Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2025 and referred to a Joint Committee of Parliament; it has not been passed.

n460beceab95.s: The ₹2,000 crore deal-value threshold for combinations under competition law targets:
n460beceab95.x: The threshold targets start-up 'killer acquisitions' that may escape traditional scrutiny; combinations are mergers and acquisitions, not cartels.

n3026e887268.s: The search-cum-selection committee for the CCI chairperson is headed by:
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Chief Justice of India or a nominee
n3026e887268.x: Chairpersons are appointed by the Central Government on a search-cum-selection committee's recommendation; for the CCI it is headed by the CJI or a nominee.

na597eec618f.s: The Securities Appellate Tribunal hears appeals against orders of SEBI, PFRDA and:
na597eec618f.x: SAT hears appeals against orders of SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA; appeals against CCI orders lie to the NCLAT.

new.s: Which financial regulator functions under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs?
new.x: IBBI is the only one of these regulators under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs; the others are under Finance.

new.s: The headquarters of IRDAI is located at:
new.x: IRDAI, set up in April 2000, is headquartered in Hyderabad; SEBI and RBI are in Mumbai.

new.s: The International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) was set up on:
new.x: IFSCA was set up on 27 April 2020 under the IFSCA Act, 2019; it is the newest financial regulator.

new.s: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) was established on 1 October 2016 under the:
new.x: IBBI is the regulator under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.

new.s: In India, the ₹1 note and coins are issued by the:
new.x: The RBI issues currency except the ₹1 note and coins, which are issued by the Ministry of Finance.

new.s: How many Upper-Layer NBFCs, including Tata Sons, did the RBI name for 2026-27?
new.x: The RBI named 17 Upper-Layer NBFCs for 2026-27; they must list within 3 years.

new.s: The RBI acts as the manager of foreign exchange under the:
new.x: The RBI is the forex manager under FEMA 1999.

new.s: Under Section 45ZN of the RBI Act, the RBI must report to the Centre if inflation stays outside the band for:
new.x: If the band is breached for 3 consecutive quarters, the RBI reports reasons, remedies and time to restore to the Centre.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee?
o: It is a statutory body under the RBI Act, 1934
The Governor chairs it and has a casting vote
It has 3 RBI members and 4 external members
new.x: The MPC has 6 members: 3 from the RBI and 3 external members appointed by the Centre for 4 years.

new.s: An appeal against an order of SEBI lies first to the:
new.x: SEBI orders go to the Securities Appellate Tribunal and then to the Supreme Court, not to the NCLAT.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about SEBI:
1. It has quasi-judicial powers to investigate, summon and impose penalties.
2. Orders of IRDAI and PFRDA are also appealable to the Securities Appellate Tribunal since 2014.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: SEBI has quasi-judicial powers, and since 2014 IRDAI and PFRDA orders also go to SAT.

new.s: In February 2025, a seven-member expert panel to review IRDAI regulations was set up under:
new.x: A seven-member panel under Dinesh Khara was set up in February 2025 to review IRDAI regulations.

new.s: IRDAI's regulation-making power comes from:
new.x: Section 114A of the Insurance Act, 1938 gives IRDAI its regulation-making power; Section 16A of the IRDA Act creates the Policyholders' fund.

new.s: IRDAI, created under the IRDA Act, 1999, was set up in:
new.x: IRDAI was set up in April 2000 under the IRDA Act, 1999; 1994 is the year of the Malhotra Committee report.

new.s: PFRDA, which worked as an interim body from 2003, became a statutory body in:
new.x: PFRDA got statutory status in 2014 under the PFRDA Act, 2013.

new.s: Chit funds in India are regulated by:
new.x: Chit funds are regulated by State governments under the Chit Funds Act 1982, not by the RBI.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a role of the Financial Stability and Development Council?
new.x: FSDC handles financial stability, inter-regulatory coordination, macro-prudential supervision and financial literacy; the repo rate is fixed by the RBI's MPC.

new.s: The Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission submitted its report in:
new.x: FSLRC, chaired by Justice B.N. Srikrishna, was set up in 2011 and reported in 2013.

new.s: The Policyholders' Education and Protection Fund under Section 16A of the IRDA Act is linked to:
new.x: Section 16A, added by the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha Act, 2025, creates the Policyholders' Education and Protection Fund under IRDAI.

new.s: The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board, under the PNGRB Act 2006, was set up on:
new.x: The PNGRB Act is of 2006, but the Board was set up on 1 October 2007.

new.s: FSSAI, under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, was set up in:
new.x: The Food Safety and Standards Act is of 2006; FSSAI was set up in 2008.

new.s: FSSAI is administered by the:
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
new.x: FSSAI is an independent statutory authority administered by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, not the DGHS.

new.s: FSSAI's Eat Right India movement was launched in:
new.x: Eat Right India (2018) is FSSAI's movement for safe, healthy and sustainable food.

new.s: Under the 2026 FSSAI reforms, basic registration covers food businesses with turnover up to:
new.x: Registration now covers turnover up to ₹1.5 crore (earlier ₹12 lakh); above ₹50 crore needs a Central licence.

new.s: Besides TRAI orders, TDSAT also hears appeals under the:
new.x: TDSAT also hears appeals under the IT Act, 2000 and the DPDP Act.

new.s: Inter-State electricity matters are regulated by the:
new.x: CERC handles inter-State electricity matters; SERCs handle intra-State tariffs.

new.s: APERC was constituted in 1999 under the:
new.x: APERC was constituted in 1999 under the AP Electricity Reform Act, 1998.

new.s: Appeals against orders of CERC, SERCs and PNGRB lie to the:
new.x: APTEL, set up on 24 August 2004 under the Electricity Act, 2003, hears appeals from CERC, SERCs and PNGRB.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about electricity regulators:
1. SERCs fix intra-State electricity tariffs.
2. Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, APERC stayed joint regulator for not more than six months.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: SERCs handle intra-State tariffs, and APERC was joint regulator for up to six months until separate SERCs were formed.

new.s: The Airports Economic Regulatory Authority (AERA) regulates:
new.x: AERA regulates airport tariffs (aeronautical charges) at major airports.

new.s: In July 2026, PNGRB approved how many Geographical Areas in Andhra Pradesh for City Gas Distribution?
new.x: PNGRB approved 10 Geographical Areas in AP for CGD; East Godavari has the most connections.

new.s: An appeal against an order of the Data Protection Board must be filed before TDSAT within:
new.x: DPB orders go to TDSAT within 60 days and then to the Supreme Court.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Data Protection Board of India?
o: It is an independent adjudicatory body
Its members are appointed on a Selection Committee's recommendation
It can impose penalties up to ₹250 crore
new.x: The Board can impose penalties up to ₹250 crore but cannot order imprisonment.

new.s: Before 26 May 2017, appeals against CCI orders lay to the:
new.x: Appeals went to COMPAT until 26 May 2017, when the NCLAT took over.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a ground for removing a regulator's chairperson?
o: Conviction for an offence of moral turpitude
new.x: Removal is by the Central Government on grounds in the parent Act, such as insolvency, moral turpitude, incapacity or abuse of position; not by Parliament.

new.s: Part XIVA (Articles 323A and 323B) was inserted into the Constitution by the:
new.x: Part XIVA was inserted by the 42nd Amendment, 1976 and came into force on 1 March 1977.

new.s: Under Article 323A, administrative tribunals for public service matters can be set up by:
new.x: Only Parliament can create a 323A tribunal; under 323B both Parliament and State Legislatures can act.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a subject listed under Article 323B?
new.x: Public service matters fall under Article 323A; taxation, land reforms and rent are Article 323B subjects.

new.s: The southern zonal bench of the National Green Tribunal is at:
new.x: NGT zonal benches are Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai (South); the principal bench is New Delhi.

new.s: An appeal against an order of the National Green Tribunal lies to the:
new.x: NGT orders are appealable directly to the Supreme Court within 90 days.

new.s: The National Green Tribunal must dispose of a case within how long of its filing?
new.x: The NGT Act mandates disposal within 6 months of filing.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Green Tribunal:
1. It became operational on 18 October 2010.
2. Its civil jurisdiction covers seven Acts listed in Schedule I.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: the NGT began on 18 October 2010 and Schedule I lists 7 Acts, including the Water Act, 1974.

new.s: In 2016, the National Green Tribunal fined the Art of Living for:
new.x: The Art of Living's World Culture Festival damaged the Yamuna floodplain, and the NGT fined it in 2016.

new.s: NCLT and NCLAT were constituted under the:
new.x: NCLT (Sec. 408) and NCLAT (Sec. 410) are under the Companies Act, 2013, not the IBC; both began on 1 June 2016.

new.s: Under Section 61 of the IBC, an appeal from the NCLT to the NCLAT must be filed within:
new.x: IBC appeals go to the NCLAT within 30 days (plus 15 days on cause); Companies Act appeals have 45 days.

new.s: The NCLAT does NOT hear appeals against orders of:
new.x: The NCLAT hears appeals from NCLT, IBBI, CCI and NFRA; SEBI orders go to the Securities Appellate Tribunal.

new.s: The Central Administrative Tribunal was set up under the:
new.x: CAT was set up under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985, made under Article 323A(1).

new.s: After L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India (1997), an appeal against a CAT order lies first to the:
o: Division Bench of the High Court
new.x: L. Chandra Kumar held judicial review under Articles 226/227 to be basic structure, so CAT orders go to a High Court Division Bench, then the Supreme Court.

new.s: Under the Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction) Rules, 2021, a District Commission hears complaints of value up to:
new.x: The District limit is up to ₹50 lakh since 2021, down from ₹1 crore.

new.s: Since 2021, the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission hears complaints of value above:
new.x: NCDRC now hears complaints above ₹2 crore (earlier above ₹10 crore).

new.s: After the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021, appeals on film certification under the Cinematograph Act, 1952 go to the:
new.x: The Act dissolved the Cinematograph Act appellate tribunal and moved its work to the High Court.

new.s: In Madras Bar Association v. Union of India (19 Nov 2025), the Supreme Court directed the Centre to set up a National Tribunals Commission within:
new.x: The Court, led by CJI B.R. Gavai, struck down re-enacted provisions and ordered a National Tribunals Commission within four months.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT dissolved by the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021?
new.x: The Act dissolved the Airport Appellate Tribunal, Customs advance rulings authority and IPAB; the NGT continues.

new.s: Legal aid is available at how many of the 23 benches of the Railway Claims Tribunal?
new.x: Legal aid is available at only 9 of the 23 Railway Claims Tribunal benches, a noted capacity gap.

new.s: A capacity gap noted for the National Green Tribunal is that it:
o: Is funded by the Ministry of Finance
new.x: The NGT has no IT division and is funded by the MoEFCC.
